ambiguities.evidence: Equation (5.3) defines Z_1=u_sG_i+(1+u_s)γ_p^r|A|, while Theorem 5.1 quantifies over i and refers back to the same Z_1 and M_1 symbols. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.3), (5.5), and Theorem 5.1]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization should treat Z_1 and M_1 as local iteration-dependent objects, or rename them Z_i and M_i while documenting that normalization; treating them as globally fixed would add an unsupported assumption. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.3), (5.5), and Theorem 5.1]
ambiguities.issue: The literal symbols Z_1 and M_1 carry subscript 1 even though Z_1 contains G_i and therefore varies with the iteration. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.3), (5.5), and Theorem 5.1]

ambiguities.evidence: The paper moves from the exact M_1 and W_i formulas to M_1=I+O(u_s), then to W_i≲… and ‖W_i‖∞≲…, before stating ‖W_i‖∞<1 in view of (5.6). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, interpretation following Theorem 5.1]
ambiguities.impact: The exact recurrence and the M-matrix bound can be formalized literally, but equation (5.7) and the asserted strict contraction require an explicit interpretation of hidden higher-order terms and constants. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, M-matrix paragraph, Theorem 5.1, and equation (5.7)]
ambiguities.issue: The symbols O(u_s) and ≲ in the interpretation of W_i have no explicit constants or quantified asymptotic regime. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, text preceding and equation (5.7)]

ambiguities.evidence: The paper says this relation can be expected in practice only after completing Theorem 5.1 and equation (5.7). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, text following equation (5.7)]
ambiguities.impact: It may motivate which term dominates the interpreted norm bound, but it must not be added to the formal source contract for Theorem 5.1. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, text following equation (5.7)]
ambiguities.issue: The statement that G_i≥|A| is presented as a practical expectation, not a theorem hypothesis or universally quantified matrix inequality. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, paragraph following equation (5.7)]

contract_plain_english: Under a componentwise correction-solver defect bound and the uniform one-half condition (5.6), a nonnegative M-matrix resolvent controls the correction contribution and yields an exact componentwise recurrence for the next true residual. The theorem includes a nonnegative additive vector y_i; only the subsequent first-order interpretation gives the approximate infinity-norm estimate (5.7), and the theorem alone does not yet bound ω. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.2)-(5.7) and Theorem 5.1]

source_evidence.observation: The paper defines cond(A), assumes the componentwise correction-solver residual bound |r̂_i−A d̂_i|≤u_sG_i|d̂_i|, and defines componentwise relative backward error ω.
For the componentwise backward-error quotient, ξ/0 is interpreted as zero when ξ=0 and as infinity otherwise.
The residual and update rounding models used in section 5 are stated componentwise.

The paper derives the base componentwise residual inequality, defines Z_1 and the M-matrix inverse M_1, proves its nonnegativity and norm bound under a one-half condition, and states the theorem's uniform hypothesis.
The theorem gives the componentwise residual recurrence with W_i and y_i, followed by a first-order interpretation of W_i and its infinity-norm bound.
The analysis ignores underflow and overflow; a scaled modification is proposed separately.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The result applies to the original unscaled Algorithm 1.1 and combines the componentwise solver-defect condition (2.5), residual computation at u_r followed by rounding to u_s, and update rounding at u. [PDF pp. 2, 5, 7, and 10-11, printed A818, A821, A823, and A826-A827, Algorithm 1.1, equations (2.5), (3.3), (3.6), and Theorem 5.1]
binders: Let A ∈ ℝ^{n×n} be nonsingular, b ∈ ℝ^n, and let Algorithm 1.1 produce x̂_i, r̂_i, d̂_i, and x̂_{i+1} for i≥0. [PDF pp. 2 and 10-11, printed A818 and A826-A827, Algorithm 1.1 and Theorem 5.1]

For each i, let G_i ∈ ℝ^{n×n} have nonnegative entries and satisfy the solver model (2.5); let I be the n×n identity. [PDF pp. 5 and 10, printed A821 and A826, equation (2.5), its explanatory text, and equations (5.3)-(5.5)]
Let p be the maximum number of nonzeros in a row of [A b], and let γ_p^r=pu_r/(1−pu_r). [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition of γ_k and text preceding equation (3.3)]
conclusions: The base inequality is |b−Ax̂_{i+1}|≤u_s|b−Ax̂_i|+(1+u_s)γ_p^r(1+u)(|b|+|A||x̂_{i+1}|)+Z_1|d̂_i|+u|A||x̂_{i+1}|. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, equation (5.2)]
Z_1=u_sG_i+(1+u_s)γ_p^r|A| and has nonnegative entries. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, equation (5.3) and following sentence]
The correction satisfies |d̂_i|≤|A^{-1}|[(1+u_s)|b−Ax̂_i|+(1+u_s)(1+u)γ_p^r(|b|+|A||x̂_{i+1}|)]+|A^{-1}|Z_1|d̂_i|. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, displayed derivation between equations (5.3) and (5.4)]

After premultiplication by Z_1, (I−Z_1|A^{-1}|)Z_1|d̂_i|≤Z_1|A^{-1}|[(1+u_s)|b−Ax̂_i|+(1+u_s)(1+u)γ_p^r(|b|+|A||x̂_{i+1}|)]. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, displayed inequality immediately before equation (5.4)]
If ‖Z_1|A^{-1}|‖∞≤1/2, then I−Z_1|A^{-1}| is an M-matrix; M_1 exists, has nonnegative entries, and satisfies ‖M_1‖∞≤2. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, paragraph following equation (5.5)]
Theorem 5.1 concludes |b−Ax̂_{i+1}|≤W_i|b−Ax̂_i|+y_i componentwise for every i≥0. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1]
W_i=u_sI+(1+u_s)M_1Z_1|A^{-1}|. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1]
y_i=(1+u_s)(1+u)γ_p^r(I+M_1Z_1|A^{-1}|)(|b|+|A||x̂_{i+1}|)+u|A||x̂_{i+1}|. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1]

For interpretation, the paper states M_1=I+O(u_s), W_i≲u_sI+(u_sG_i+γ_p^r|A|)|A^{-1}|, and ‖W_i‖∞≲u_s+u_s‖G_i|A^{-1}|‖∞+γ_p^r cond(A^{-1}). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, text preceding and equation (5.7)]

The paper then states ‖W_i‖∞<1 in view of (5.6) and concludes that ‖W_i‖∞ is much less than one when the solver is not too unstable and A is not too ill conditioned relative to u_s. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, text following equation (5.7)]
constants_and_indexing: Theorem 5.1 requires condition (5.6) for all i and concludes the recurrence for every i≥0. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equation (5.6) and continuation of Theorem 5.1]
The M-matrix threshold is exactly 1/2, and the resulting resolvent norm bound is exactly 2. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, paragraph following equation (5.5)]
The factors (1+u_s)(1+u) multiply γ_p^r in y_i, while W_i contains (1+u_s)M_1Z_1|A^{-1}|. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, formulas for W_i and y_i]
Although denoted Z_1 and M_1, both quantities depend on the current i through G_i. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.3), (5.5), and Theorem 5.1]
definitions_and_conventions: All absolute values of vectors and matrices are entrywise, and all displayed vector and matrix inequalities are componentwise. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, section 2 notation]
For nonsingular B, cond(B)=‖|B^{-1}||B|‖∞; hence cond(A^{-1})=‖|A||A^{-1}|‖∞, with the multiplication order shown. [PDF pp. 5 and 10, printed A821 and A826, equation (2.2) and equation (5.6)]

Z_1 and M_1 are the literal symbols used in equations (5.3) and (5.5), while W_i and y_i are the theorem's iteration-indexed matrix and vector. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.3), (5.5), and Theorem 5.1]

The componentwise relative backward error is ω(y)=max_j |b−Ay|_j/(|A||y|+|b|)_j, equivalently the minimum common componentwise relative perturbation to A and b. [PDF pp. 5-6, printed A821-A822, equations (2.6) and (2.7)]
error_notions: The theorem's main conclusion is a componentwise recurrence for the exact residual |b−Ax̂_i|, not directly a bound on ω(x̂_i). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 and the discussion after equation (5.7)]

The computed residual r̂_i appears in the solver hypothesis, while the theorem recurrence uses the exact original-system residual b−Ax̂_i. [PDF pp. 5 and 11, printed A821 and A827, equation (2.5) and Theorem 5.1]

The additive vector y_i is explicitly noted not to be a scalar multiple of |A||x̂_{i+1}|+|b|, so an ω bound requires the later Lemma 5.2 argument rather than following immediately from Theorem 5.1. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, paragraph after equation (5.7)]
exceptional_values: Condition (5.6) ensures the inverse defining M_1 exists and is nonnegative; without such a condition, equation (5.5) alone does not guarantee an admissible componentwise resolvent. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, equations (5.5), (5.6), and the M-matrix paragraph]
For ω, a zero denominator component is interpreted as zero only when the corresponding numerator is zero and as infinity otherwise. [PDF p. 6, printed A822, continuation of equation (2.7)]
The finite γ_p^r bound implicitly needs the ordinary standard-model smallness condition on pu_r. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition and use of γ_p^r]
Underflow and overflow are ignored; the scaled algorithm introduced in section 6 is not part of Theorem 5.1. [PDF p. 12, printed A828, section 6, Scaling]
higher_order_terms: Equations (5.2)-(5.6) and the W_i,y_i recurrence are exact inequalities with no omitted big-O terms. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.2)-(5.6) and Theorem 5.1]

The later statement M_1=I+O(u_s) and both ≲ bounds suppress higher-order terms and unspecified constants; equation (5.7) is therefore an interpretation, not the exact theorem recurrence. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, text preceding and equation (5.7)]
hypotheses: The step-4 solver satisfies |r̂_i−A d̂_i|≤u_sG_i|d̂_i| componentwise. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, equation (2.5)]
For all i, u_s‖G_i|A^{-1}|‖∞+(1+u_s)γ_p^r cond(A^{-1})≤1/2. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equation (5.6) and its continuation]
The residual and update satisfy the componentwise models (3.3) and (3.6). [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equations (3.3) and (3.6)]
The unit roundoffs inherit u_r≤u≤u_s≤u_f from Algorithm 1.1. [PDF pp. 1-2, printed A817-A818, equation (1.1) and the definition of u_s]
implicit_context: Equation (5.1), |x̂_i|≤(1+u)|x̂_{i+1}|+|d̂_i|, is used to replace x̂_i by x̂_{i+1} and d̂_i in the derivation of (5.2) and (5.4). [PDF p. 10, printed A826, equation (5.1) and following derivation]

Condition (5.6) is a scalar sufficient condition for ‖Z_1|A^{-1}|‖∞≤1/2 because Z_1=u_sG_i+(1+u_s)γ_p^r|A| and cond(A^{-1})=‖|A||A^{-1}|‖∞. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, equations (5.3), (5.5), and (5.6)]

W_i and y_i are nonnegative componentwise under the theorem's M-matrix conclusion, although the theorem does not separately label this fact. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, nonnegativity discussion after (5.5) and formulas for W_i and y_i]
The practical expectation G_i≥|A| appears only after the theorem and is not one of Theorem 5.1's assumptions. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, paragraph following equation (5.7)]
norms: The recurrence and its base inequalities are componentwise; only the hypotheses establishing the M-matrix and the interpretation (5.7) use the infinity norm. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.2)-(5.7)]
The matrix condition in (5.6) uses cond(A^{-1}), not cond(A) or κ∞(A). [PDF p. 10, printed A826, equation (5.6)]
The M-matrix resolvent bound is ‖M_1‖∞≤2 under the exact threshold ‖Z_1|A^{-1}|‖∞≤1/2. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, paragraph following equation (5.5)]
numerical_model: Residual computation contributes γ_p^r and residual rounding contributes u_s and 1+u_s; update rounding contributes u and 1+u. [PDF pp. 7 and 10-11, printed A823 and A826-A827, equations (3.3), (3.6), (5.1)-(5.4), and Theorem 5.1]

The solver model (2.5) is componentwise and permits an iteration-dependent nonnegative matrix G_i rather than a scalar normwise constant. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, equation (2.5) and its explanatory text]
The exact theorem recurrence retains all displayed finite-precision factors; the subsequent W_i interpretation is asymptotic. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, Theorem 5.1 and equation (5.7)]

undebatable_constraints: The solver premise is the componentwise inequality (2.5) with a nonnegative matrix G_i. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, equation (2.5) and following text]
Condition (5.6) is uniform over all i and contains cond(A^{-1}) with the order |A||A^{-1}|. [PDF pp. 5 and 10-11, printed A821 and A826-A827, equation (2.2), equation (5.6), and its continuation]
The exact theorem conclusion includes both W_i and the additive vector y_i; omitting y_i changes the result. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1]
The products M_1Z_1|A^{-1}|, |A||x̂_{i+1}|, and G_i|A^{-1}| have fixed, noncommutative order. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.4)-(5.7) and Theorem 5.1]
Equation (5.7) is an infinity-norm asymptotic interpretation and must not replace the exact componentwise recurrence. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 and equation (5.7)]
The theorem itself does not claim a componentwise relative backward-error bound for ω; that requires the subsequent lemma and analysis. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, discussion following equation (5.7)]
